definitions.explanation: describes a claim, rumor, or accusation that has absolutely no basis in fact

examples.japanese: その{噂|うわさ}は{事実無根|じじつむこん}だ。
{事実無根|じじつむこん}の{報道|ほうどう}に{対|たい}して{抗議|こうぎ}した。
examples.english: I protested against the baseless reporting.

examples.japanese: {弁護士|べんごし}は「{依頼人|いらいにん}に{対|たい}する{告発|こくはつ}は{事実無根|じじつむこん}である」と{声明|せいめい}を{出|だ}した。
examples.english: The lawyer issued a statement saying the accusations against his client are utterly unfounded.

notes:
A formal four-character compound ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}) frequently used in news, legal contexts, and public denials. It is a strong, emphatic way to deny something — stronger than simply saying {嘘|うそ} (lie) because it asserts a complete absence of factual basis.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {事実無根|じじつむこん}の{噂|うわさ}: a baseless rumor
- {事実無根|じじつむこん}の{報道|ほうどう}: groundless reporting
- {事実無根|じじつむこん}であると{主張|しゅちょう}する: to claim something is groundless
- {事実無根|じじつむこん}の{誹謗中傷|ひぼうちゅうしょう}: baseless slander

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {根拠|こんきょ}がない: has no basis — simpler and less formal
- {根|ね}も{葉|は}もない: completely unfounded — idiomatic, used in conversation
- {荒唐無稽|こうとうむけい}: absurd, preposterous — emphasizes ridiculousness rather than falsehood
- {濡|ぬ}れ{衣|ぎぬ}: false accusation — focuses on being wrongly blamed

ETYMOLOGY:
{事実|じじつ} (fact) + {無根|むこん} (without root/basis). Literally: "fact-rootless" — there is no factual root to the claim.
